A small rehearsal room, sealed off during an earlier renovation, still held a working radio. Nobody could explain who had left it there. The discovery made a good newspaper story. What mattered more to the local choir was the room itself: dry, bright, and just large enough for a dozen voices.
difficulty_variants.instruction: Read once to one interested listener. Identify the change or discovery in the story, and let it shape your pace and emphasis. Use your natural voice, then listen back before moving on.
difficulty_variants.reflection_prompt: Where did the story change? Could you hear that turn in your delivery?

difficulty_variants.label: The final correction
difficulty_variants.text: The guidebook was ready to print when an elderly reader returned a marked copy. Most corrections were small: a spelling, a date, the name of a shop. One note changed a larger story. The person credited with saving the village records had not worked alone. Three neighbors had carried the boxes out together. The editor added their names and delayed the printing by a day. It was a correction worth making.
